findings.title: Microphone and conversation data require explicit privacy and consent controls
findings.impact: Starting capture without clear notice, retaining raw audio, persisting transcripts by default, or speaking responses without opt-in could expose sensitive conversation content and create inaccessible or surprising behavior.
evidence: STEP-003 requires consent and privacy analysis before microphone or cloud use.
The approved defaults are no raw-audio retention, session-only transcripts, disabled transcript analytics, and spoken responses off until explicit opt-in.
The browser must expose listening, transcript, correction, cancellation, permission-denied, unavailable, and fallback states.
findings.resolution: Require concise notice before permission, an affirmative microphone action, a persistent visible listening indicator, immediate stop and cancel controls, transcript correction before endpoint acceptance, session expiry deletion, no raw-audio persistence, no content logs, spoken output opt-in per session, and equivalent keyboard, screen-reader, reduced-motion, text-only, and guided-only paths.

findings.title: Grounding and generated output remain untrusted across the model boundary
findings.impact: User transcripts or retrieved documents could attempt to override policy, request unavailable actions, disclose hidden context, or produce unsafe and unsupported claims.
evidence: STEP-003 requires prompt-injection and output-safety controls.
STEP-008 requires approved versioned sources, citations, explicit unknowns, stale-source handling, and output validation.
No web grounding, external content retrieval, or model processing is authorized in Steps 1-4.
findings.resolution: Separate instructions from user and retrieved data; allowlist corpus manifests; cap and normalize inputs; treat retrieved instructions as inert text; restrict tools and actions to none for informational turns; validate response schema, capability claims, citations, corpus version, and URLs; run content safety on input and output when a provider is later approved; fail to explicit unknown, refusal, or guided fallback on injection, unsupported claims, unsafe content, stale sources, or validator failure.

findings.title: Session identity, authorization, and secrets must terminate at the server boundary
findings.impact: Browser credentials, cross-session event replay, over-broad service roles, or unauthenticated reconnect could expose conversations or permit another user to resume, cancel, or confirm a turn.
evidence: STEP-002 separates browser and server sessions and requires cancellation and reconnect contracts.
STEP-003 requires authentication, least-privilege RBAC, and server secret controls.
The architecture assigns service credentials, grounding policy, and privileged adapters exclusively to the server.
findings.resolution: Authenticate before session creation; authorize every event against user, session, turn, and intended operation; use unguessable short-lived session and resume tokens bound to identity and last acknowledged sequence; reject replay and cross-session IDs; require explicit confirmation for consequential actions; keep credentials in server-managed identity or secret storage; prohibit browser secrets and log redaction; scope future AzureUSGovernment RBAC to the minimum data-plane actions and resource boundary.

findings.title: Abuse and dependency failures need bounded rate, retry, health, and telemetry behavior
findings.impact: Unbounded utterances, sessions, retries, reconnects, or response streams can amplify cost and denial of service, while content-rich logs can leak transcripts, prompts, retrieved text, responses, credentials, or authorization metadata.
evidence: STEP-003 requires rate limits, bounded retries, health, metrics, and redacted structured logs.
STEP-004 requires deterministic service-unavailable, reconnect, cost, and fallback outcomes.
Session-only transcripts and no raw-audio retention prohibit routine conversation-content telemetry.
findings.resolution: Enforce per-identity and per-session concurrency, utterance duration, event size, turn rate, token/output, reconnect, and daily cost ceilings; use deadlines and at most two transient retries with jitter and Retry-After; open a circuit after repeated dependency failure; expose liveness and readiness; propagate cancellation; log only pseudonymous correlation IDs, state, duration bucket, error category, retry count, rate decision, correction, cancellation, reconnect, citation count, and fallback without conversation or secret content.

findings.title: Independent human review is not enforced for source changes
findings.impact: A compromised or mistaken sole maintainer can submit code that passes automated checks without a second person reviewing design intent, trust boundaries, or release consequences.
findings.exploitPath: The sole write-capable administrator submits a change that satisfies automated checks but contains a human-reviewable logic or governance defect; no approving reviewer is required before merge.
evidence: Main requires strict Aggregate cross-platform evidence and JavaScript security analysis checks with admin enforcement.
Force pushes and deletions are disabled; linear history and conversation resolution are required.
Secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot security updates, vulnerability alerts, automated fixes, and private vulnerability reporting are enabled.
Actions are restricted to GitHub-owned actions, CodeQL has zero open alerts, but required pull-request reviews are unset because only one write-capable collaborator exists.
findings.resolution: Provision a distinct qualified collaborator or team, require at least one approving review, and assign CODEOWNERS to security-sensitive source; retain separately signed independent release review.
references: GitHub REST read-only repository evidence collected 2026-09-05

limitations: This is a pre-implementation threat model; controls are requirements and are not claimed as implemented or tested.
No credential, secret, source change, runtime, browser, model, Speech service, network, Azure environment, or deployed endpoint was inspected or exercised.
Content-safety capability and AzureUSGovernment availability remain unknown until separately approved discovery; no provider was selected.
SECF-0205 is preserved as unrelated current-project security history and is not a LIVE-CHAT-001 defect.
A signed independent review must come from a distinct trusted reviewer; this assessment does not satisfy that release gate.
